title: ICE’s Operation Predator and Victim Identification FY15 Statistics
description: More than 1,000 victims of child sexual abuse and online exploitation were identified or rescued in fiscal year 2015, as part of child exploitation investigations conducted by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s (ICE) Homeland Security Investigations (HSI).

transcript.text: Cyber Crime Center is HSI's collaborative effort to pool all of our resources and focus on cyber-related
investigations and crime, cyber-enabled crimes to include child exploitation but also to include
other types of investigations where a computer or the internet is used to facilitate the
commission of a crime.
What we're announcing today are the results of a year-long effort by our agents in the
field as well as our agents here at C3 to combat child sexual exploitation by locating, identifying
and rescuing victims and bringing their perpetrators to justice.
HSI has a long history of combating child exploitation going all the way back to when we were the
U.S. Customs Service and when child exploitation materials were predated the internet and were
smuggled into the United States illicitly through various ports of entry and printed form.
We have taken that expertise and through the 90s with the emergence of the internet and the
proliferation of child exploitation we have made it a focus and a top priority of our agency
to combat child exploitation.
Since the 21st century and the continued expansion of technology worldwide unfortunately child pornography
has also grown exponentially and so our efforts have redoubled and we've committed our resources
significantly to combating this major issue.
My name is James Cole and I'm the National Program Manager for Victim Identification at
the Cyber Crime Center with Homeland Security Investigations.
So here we manage the victim identification laboratory.
Within that laboratory our goal is to conduct image, video and audio analysis, enhancements
and clarifications of child exploitation material with the goal of identifying and rescuing the
child victims, identifying and apprehending the offenders, identifying and locating the
crime scene.
We use a host of technology, hardware, software tools to conduct that analysis including Photoshop,
Premiere Pro and other Adobe products, real workhorse products that are specific to forensics
like motion DSPs like Kenneth Forensic and we also analyze large volumes of image and
video material related to child exploitation using GRIFI analyze digital investigator.
The goal here is really to identify and rescue child victims.
From doing that work the arrests and the convictions come but the main purpose of this program
is to identify and rescue child victims.
Also work that we've done as a result of this laboratory has influenced the way that the agency
as a whole approaches these investigations in the field and so as a result over the last
four years we've seen a tremendous uptick in the amount of victims that we're identifying
and rescuing in the field.
In 2014 we identified and rescued 1036 child victims in the course of the year and in 2015
we identified and rescued 1004 victims.
We've gone through a paradigm shift with an HSI which is really going from being a fender
focus to victim focus with our investigations and our computer forensics.
What we have found is when you focus on victims you will find offenders as well but when you
focus on offenders you don't necessarily find the victims.
